papers.title: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods. We reimagine PSS for LLMs as a sequential process over the whole stream and propose RICoT (Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought), a prompting framework that works through the pages as a reader would: within a sliding window it reasons about each page and commits its boundary decision before moving on, and across windows it carries forward a compact record of what it has read, keeping per-call cost bounded. We also introduce FinancePSS-205, a benchmark of 205 real-world, de-identified financial page streams, to be released publicly. On FinancePSS-205, RICoT matches or outperforms pairwise and windowed prompting with the same backbone for each of three open-weight LLMs; on a TABME test subset, RICoT with GLM-5 reaches document F1 0.847 and boundary F1 0.915, above published zero-shot results. A 2B-parameter student, trained on a larger teacher's decisions with and without the page-level reasoning, performs comparably in both modes and comes within 0.05 document F1 of the strongest prompted model on FinancePSS-205.
papers.title_zh: RICoT：用于页面流分割的循环交错思维链
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）重新激发了人们对页面流分割（PSS）的兴趣，该任务旨在将一个多页文件拆分为其构成的各个文档。然而，已发表的 LLM 方法仍将该任务设定为对一个或少数相邻页面的边界分类，而商业文档拆分 API 并不公开其方法。我们将面向 LLM 的 PSS 重新设想为对整个流的顺序处理过程，并提出 RICoT（循环交错思维链），这是一个像读者一样逐页推进的提示框架：在滑动窗口内，它对每一页进行推理，并在继续前进之前做出其边界决策；跨窗口时，它向前传递其所读内容的紧凑记录，使每次调用的成本保持有界。我们还提出了 FinancePSS-205，这是一个包含 205 条真实世界、去标识化金融页面流的基准，将公开发布。在 FinancePSS-205 上，对于三个开放权重 LLM 中的每一个，RICoT 在使用相同骨干模型的情况下匹配或优于成对提示与窗口提示；在 TABME 测试子集上，使用 GLM-5 的 RICoT 达到文档 F1 0.847 和边界 F1 0.915，高于已发表的零样本结果。一个 2B 参数的学生模型，在带有和不带有页面级推理的情况下基于更大教师模型的决策进行训练，在两种模式下表现相当，并在 FinancePSS-205 上以 0.05 文档 F1 之差接近最强的提示模型。

papers.title: LMMR: Learned Multigranular Memory Retrieval for Small Language Model Agents
papers.summary: Small language model agents have limited space to read the memory needed for multi-hop questions. Relevant facts are often scattered across records whose surrounding text consumes much of that space. We propose LMMR, a learned multigranular memory retrieval method that selects both the next source and how much of it to read. LMMR links paragraphs and sentence fragments to their original sources and pairs views that supply the same missing support during training. Relevant distractors and repeated information provide contrasting examples. At inference, the reranker scores what each candidate adds to an anchor passage, and a selector chooses the evidence within a token budget. On 22,398 official validation questions from HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, and MuSiQue, a frozen 2B answer model reaches 61.47, 43.26, and 30.58 F1 under a 400-token budget. The gains over query expansion are 3.06, 2.14, and 4.55 points, while memory input decreases by 23.1-26.9%. LMMR also uses 23.5-27.7% fewer input tokens than a coarse retriever trained on the same questions. Against that retriever followed by LLMLingua-2 at comparable input lengths, F1 gains reach 3.99 points and are significant on HotpotQA and 2WikiMultihopQA after Holm correction. All eight small answer models evaluated on HotpotQA improve over query expansion and MMR in both F1 and exact match.

papers.title: Growing Clusters Lower the Bar: Profile Accretion in LLM-Based Incremental Entity Resolution
papers.summary: Incremental entity resolution pipelines ask a large language model (LLM) whether a new record belongs to an existing cluster and show it the records already linked. Analyses of matching oracles assume that the answer depends only on the records compared. For the LLM matchers we test, it depends on cluster size, and the model lowers its bar for joining a cluster as the cluster grows. On French procurement suppliers from FOPPA, with SIREN identifiers as ground truth, we hold the new record fixed and vary only the number of verified members shown. Sixteen members instead of one raise the false match rate on similarly named companies by \dfmrMin--\dfmrMax{} percentage points in six open-weight models, while their area under the ROC curve rises by only \aucGainMin--\aucGainMax. In Claude Sonnet~5 and Haiku~5.5 the rise is \clSonD{} and \clHaiD{} points. The shift persists with street addresses, prompt variants and the BatchER and ComEM formats, and one false merge raises acceptance of the intruder's other records in every open model. It does not arise on Czech and Bulgarian TED notices, where one record with its full address already identifies the company. In online linking on confusable blocks, a single threshold set on labelled data raises recall by a factor of \fxRRmin--\fxRRmax{} for five models with no detectable loss of precision and no extra LLM calls.
papers.title_zh: 不断增长的簇降低门槛：基于LLM的增量实体解析中的画像累积
papers.abstract_zh: 增量实体解析流水线询问大语言模型（LLM）一条新记录是否属于一个已有簇，并向其展示已经链接的记录。对匹配预言机的分析假设答案仅取决于所比较的记录。对于我们测试的LLM匹配器，答案取决于簇大小，并且随着簇增长，模型会降低加入该簇的门槛。在来自FOPPA的法国采购供应商上，以SIREN标识符作为真值，我们固定新记录不变，仅改变所展示的已验证成员数量。与只展示一个成员相比，展示十六个成员使六个开放权重模型中对名称相似公司的误匹配率提高\dfmrMin--\dfmrMax{}个百分点，而它们的ROC曲线下面积仅提高\aucGainMin--\aucGainMax。在Claude Sonnet~5和Haiku~5.5中，上升幅度分别为\clSonD{}和\clHaiD{}个点。这种偏移在街道地址、提示变体以及BatchER和ComEM格式下依然存在，并且在每个开放模型中，一次错误合并都会提高对入侵者其他记录的接受度。它在捷克和保加利亚的TED公告中并未出现，因为在那里一条带有完整地址的记录已经能够识别该公司。在易混淆块上的在线链接中，在标注数据上设置的单一阈值使五个模型的召回率提高为原来的\fxRRmin--\fxRRmax{}倍，且未检测到精确率损失，也没有额外的LLM调用。

papers.title: From syllable representation via gesture generation to articulation: A spiking neural model
papers.summary: Speech production requires a transformation from phonological representations into coordinated vocal-tract movements. This paper presents a spiking neural sensorimotor model within the Neural Engineering Framework and Semantic Pointer Architecture. Each syllable occurrence has a neural oscillator whose evolving phase coordinates its gestures and initiates the next syllable. Phase-dependent commands recruit separate neural populations for vocalic, oral-constriction, velopharyngeal, and glottal actions (gestures). Neural ramp integrators shape the rise and fall of gesture activation. Together with articulatory targets, these trajectories determine the extent and time course of articulatory movements. Opponent neural populations provide control signals to a geometric articulatory model. Thirty reference recordings cover an input corpus of eight lexical words, an alternative realization of one word, a syllable sequence, and isolated syllables. Two additional paired simulation subcorpora of sixty runs each, covering two words and one syllable sequence, assess activation reliability across neural realizations. Adjusting gesture command amplitudes increased successful realizations from 57/60 to 60/60 under the specified criteria, with ramp rate factors held constant. The model demonstrates how neural oscillator and ramp dynamics generate articulatory timing under specified phasing rules. It complements a preceding mental-lexicon model through an ordered syllable interface. Continuous online execution across all components and connection to the acoustic extension remain further integration steps. Accessible code and synchronized visualization support inspection of the neural activation trajectories and resulting vocal-tract movements.

papers.title: MM-ReportBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Report Generation from Tables
papers.summary: The ability to generate multimodal reports integrating fluent narratives with faithful visualizations from tabular data, has become a cornerstone capability for modern vision-language models in practical domains such as finance, healthcare, and policy making. However, existing benchmarks are limited by single-modality focus, simplistic metrics, novelty evaluation, and visualization quality. We address these limitations with MM-ReportBench, a multimodal report evaluation benchmark covering 386 tasks across 185 real-world tables. Each task is paired with an expert-curated reference report featuring standardized chapter structures and verifiable key insight points, constructed through a hybrid pipeline of multimodal reports generation based on Monte Carlo Tree Search and rigorous human quality control. For robust evaluation, we design a dual-judge evaluation framework: Text Judge Model assesses textual quality along structural completeness, grounded insight verification with numerical fact-checking against source tables, and novelty analysis that distinguishes genuine analytical discovery from trivial paraphrasing; Visualization Judge Model evaluates generated visualizations across data fidelity, expressiveness, aesthetics, and technical correctness. They also evaluate cross-modal consistency. Extensive experiments on 20 state-of-the-art models reveal critical weaknesses: even the strongest model achieves only 68.9 overall score, with numerical hallucination affecting 38.5% of reports and genuinely novel insights remaining rare. Our ablation studies further demonstrate that single-judge evaluation consistently inflates scores by 8-12 points compared to dual-judge assessment, confirming that rigorous and reliable benchmarking demands multi-faceted, complementary evaluation probes.

papers.title: JET: Just-Enough Exploration Tuning for Efficient Tool-Calling Agents in Repository-Level Question Answering
papers.summary: In repository-level question answering (QA), an agent explores a code repository with tools and should answer a question once enough information is gathered. Nevertheless, we find that LLM agents often continue to invoke tools even after the gathered information is already sufficient to answer. We call this phenomenon over-exploration. Moreover, even though existing methods improve task performance through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on expert trajectories, SFT also propagates the over-exploration in the trajectories to the agent. To mitigate over-exploration, we propose Just-Enough Exploration Tuning (JET), a fine-tuning method that trains the agent to answer once the gathered information is sufficient. JET truncates each training trajectory at the step where the gathered information becomes sufficient, inserts a rationale that explains why the agent can answer at that step, and fine-tunes the agent with a higher loss weight on the rationale. Experiments on two repository-level QA benchmarks with two open-weight 8B models demonstrate that JET reduces tool calls by 11 to 33% on self-generated trajectories while largely preserving the score. On expert trajectories, JET makes 18 to 28% fewer tool calls than SFT while retaining most of the score gain of SFT. In both cases, JET also lowers the inference cost.

papers.title: AfriNORM: An Evaluation Benchmark for Normative Reasoning of LLMs Across African Cultures
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across various sectors. However, current evaluation benchmarks are insufficient to assess the applicability of these models in local African contexts, as most focus on linguistic fluency (grammar/translation) rather than cultural competence. The few existing benchmarks that measure general knowledge or social conventions do not capture the African deontic modality, i.e., the strict norms and taboos that govern diverse social interactions. In this paper, we introduce AfriNORM, a scenario-based, multiple-choice question dataset designed to measure and diagnose the normative reasoning limitations of LLMs when applied to African sociocultural contexts. We introduce two metrics: a Universal Commonsense Bias Score (UCBS) to quantify commonsense bias in LLM and a Distractor Bias Score (DBS) to quantify an LLM's limited understanding of African cultural norms. We also conduct a case study on the Yorùbá language, identifying confusion gaps in two closed-source LLMs, "Gemini 2.0 Flash" and "GPT-5", and one open-source LLM, "Llama 3.1 8B Instruct" when prompted in English versus Yorùbá. While their accuracy in English is high, their performance in Yorùbá is much lower, attributable to cultural confusion rather than simple bias, indicating that the models exhibit semantic confusion when reasoning about norms in Yorùbá.
papers.title_zh: AfriNORM：面向非洲文化的大语言模型规范性推理评测基准
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）正日益被部署到各个领域。然而，当前的评测基准不足以评估这些模型在非洲本地情境中的适用性，因为大多数基准关注的是语言流畅性（语法/翻译），而非文化能力。少数现有的、衡量常识或社会习俗的基准并未捕捉到非洲的道义情态，即支配多样社会互动的严格规范和禁忌。在本文中，我们提出 AfriNORM，一个基于情境的多项选择题数据集，旨在衡量并诊断大型语言模型应用于非洲社会文化情境时的规范性推理局限。我们引入两个指标：通用常识偏差分数（UCBS），用于量化大型语言模型中的常识偏差；以及干扰项偏差分数（DBS），用于量化大型语言模型对非洲文化规范理解的局限性。我们还对约鲁巴语（Yorùbá）进行了案例研究，识别出两个闭源大型语言模型“Gemini 2.0 Flash”和“GPT-5”以及一个开源大型语言模型“Llama 3.1 8B Instruct”在使用英语与约鲁巴语提示时存在的混淆差距。尽管它们在英语上的准确率很高，但在约鲁巴语上的表现却低得多，这可归因于文化混淆而非简单的偏差，表明这些模型在就约鲁巴语中的规范进行推理时表现出语义混淆。

papers.title: Understanding Cross-Modal Inconsistency through Representation Subspaces in Omni Models
papers.summary: Omni Models process audio, vision, and text within a unified language backbone, yet often produce different answers for semantically equivalent inputs across modalities. Existing representation-level analyses do not distinguish between information that predicts whether disagreement will occur and the representation whose perturbation affects the model's answer. In this paper, we estimate a low-dimensional Answer Subspace from answer-position representations and use it to separate answer-related components from the remaining representation. Across three Omni Models and two multimodal reasoning tasks, information predictive of cross-modal inconsistency lies mainly outside the Answer Subspace, concentrating in a reproducible two-dimensional representation that is not explained by a fixed modality offset. Matched interventions reveal distinct behavioral roles: perturbing the Answer Subspace substantially changes the model's predictions, whereas perturbing the disagreement representation, like a random subspace of the same dimensionality, leaves them almost unchanged. Our key finding is that cross-modal disagreement can be induced by misaligning modality-specific answer representations: perturbing the Answer Subspace for only one modality induces disagreement, whereas applying the same perturbation to both largely preserves agreement. Thus, the representation that predicts disagreement is distinct from the answer-level representation through which disagreement can be induced, showing that linear decodability does not imply behavioral efficacy.

papers.title: Contract-Explicit Evaluation: From Auditing Learned Readers to Scoped Certificates
papers.summary: Evaluation readings of document-level relation extraction (DocRE) systems depend jointly on the model and the evaluation contract: gold version, scoring function, threshold. Rankings reverse across contracts, yet no existing method determines which comparisons survive the reversal. We address this gap with contract-explicit evaluation: a preregistered five-step protocol (Declare, Measure, Scope, Certify, Hedge), operationalizing the classical concordance decomposition of Kendall's rank correlation, that scopes certifiable regions and delivers distribution-free census certificates across two ecosystems. In the DocRE audit (44 training runs of one in-house architecture family), the scoring dimension scopes to a census certificate (three flagged instances, Clopper--Pearson upper bound 0.146); the confirmatory record includes registered negatives, and the audit prices its own simplification finding---the calibration dial's entire margin is one withdrawn commit. In an LLM-judge census (17 judges, 49,938 battles), 12.25% of leaderboard comparisons require hedging at the pre-declared split criterion (bound 0.124; panel-robust 0.143), with an exploratory two-tier reading certifying 69% at a bound \le 0.072 and a validity decomposition against released human labels (65% of contested battles are judge error, not ambiguity). The cross-model certificate is withdrawn on real confidence scores; the failure spectrum maps the boundary. The protocol, map, ledger, and per-instance artifacts are released.

papers.title: Visibility Graph Representations of Word Embeddings for Text Classification
papers.summary: Text classifiers depend on representations that expose the distinctions between classes in a form the learning model can use, and a restricted vocabulary changes which representation is most effective. This paper studies natural visibility graphs as an intermediate representation for news topic classification under controlled vocabulary budgets. Word embeddings are averaged into a fixed-length document vector, the vector is read as an ordered numerical series, and its natural visibility graph is passed to a classifier either as an ordered node-degree vector or as an adjacency matrix. On the four-class AG News benchmark, chi-square selection retains 100 to 1,500 words, and the graph inputs are compared with direct embedding-based representations from continuous bag-of-words, skip-gram, GloVe, FastText and BERT. With a fully connected classifier, the degree representation is the most accurate configuration from 700 selected words onward; it reaches its highest accuracy of 91.24% at 1,000 words and exceeds the BERT-based baseline by 0.29 percentage points at 1,500 words. In a separate convolutional comparison, the adjacency input reaches 86.16% at 1,000 words, against 83.12% for the strongest static embedding. The results indicate that visibility-derived features can be competitive once the selected vocabulary provides adequate coverage. We discuss the roles of graph compression, coordinate ordering and classifier choice, and the controls needed to establish the reliability of the small differences observed.

papers.title: Route Optimization under Port Congestion and Carbon Reduction: An NSGA-II Approach
papers.summary: Maritime shipping simultaneously faces the dual challenges of escalating port congestion and increasingly stringent decarbonization mandates. Large-scale vessel anchorage at hub ports inflates unit transport costs while generating significant additional \(CO_2\) emissions from idling auxiliary engines. This study develops a multi-objective routing optimization framework that jointly incorporates time, transport, and carbon emission costs under congestion-dependent generalized cost functions. A variational inequality (VI) model is formulated to characterize network equilibrium in vessel route allocation, while the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is deployed to solve the resulting three-objective optimization problem. The model is empirically validated using China's coastal container network (Shanghai as the primary congested port, Ningbo-Zhoushan as the backup alternative), with sensitivity analyses conducted across congestion levels, carbon tax rates, and fuel price differentials. Key findings indicate that: (1) alternative ports effectively hedge congestion when diversion costs fall below waiting costs, with a diversion threshold at approximately 60 vessel calls; (2) a carbon tax of 80/t \(CO_2\) pushes clean fuel adoption above 50%; and (3) fuel prices primarily influence energy-type selection rather than port diversion decisions, confirming that the two decision dimensions operate independently. These findings offer actionable decision support for port authorities, regulators, and shipping operators seeking to balance economic efficiency with environmental sustainability.

papers.title: Cross-cultural Adaptation of Recipes for Low-Resource Languages: A Benchmark and Multilingual Culinary Lexicon for Hausa, Yorùbá, and Igbo
papers.summary: Recent multilingual large language models (LLMs) have improved machine translation, yet culturally adaptive translation for low-resource languages (LRLs) remains underexplored. This is particularly challenging for recipes, where ingredients, cooking tools, measurements, and procedures may require adaptation to the target cultural context. In this work, we introduce ReciLoReL, a benchmark of 600 expert-translated and culturally adapted recipes across Yorùbá, Hausa, and Igbo (three of the most prominent languages in Nigeria), and ReciLex, a multilingual culinary lexicon containing approximately 15,000 translated entities across ten recipe entity categories, including ingredients, tools, chef actions, state of tools, and durations. We evaluate state-of-the-art multilingual LLMs for English-to-LRL recipe translation under zero-shot and few-shot settings and investigate whether augmenting LLMs with ReciLex improves culturally adaptive recipe translation without requiring large target-language recipe corpora for training or fine-tuning. Beyond conventional reference-based translation evaluation using BLEU, chrF, and TER, we introduce five criteria for evaluating cultural adaptation, adapted from established cross-cultural adaptation methods. Across the selected LLMs and languages, ReciLex improves average BLEU from 13.57 to 14.51 and chrF from 37.89 to 38.74, while reducing TER from 77.14 to 75.12. Human evaluation further shows improvements ranging from 0.11 to 0.36 points across the five cultural adaptation evaluation criteria on a five-point scale. Overall, our work provides new resources, evaluation criteria, and empirical evaluation for studying culturally adaptive recipe translation in low-resource settings.
papers.title_zh: 低资源语言食谱的跨文化适配：面向豪萨语、约鲁巴语和伊博语的基准与多语言烹饪词典
papers.abstract_zh: 近期的多语言大语言模型（LLMs）改进了机器翻译，但面向低资源语言（LRLs）的文化适配翻译仍未被充分探索。这对食谱而言尤其具有挑战性，因为食材、烹饪工具、计量方式和操作步骤可能需要适配目标文化语境。在本工作中，我们引入 ReciLoReL，一个包含 600 份经专家翻译并完成文化适配的食谱基准，覆盖约鲁巴语、豪萨语和伊博语（尼日利亚三种最突出的语言），以及 ReciLex，一个多语言烹饪词典，包含跨十个食谱实体类别、约 15,000 个已翻译实体，类别包括食材、工具、厨师动作、工具状态和时长。我们在零样本和少样本设置下评估最先进的多语言 LLMs 在英语到低资源语言食谱翻译中的表现，并研究在不要求大规模目标语言食谱语料用于训练或微调的情况下，用 ReciLex 增强 LLMs 是否能改善文化适配的食谱翻译。除使用 BLEU、chrF 和 TER 的常规基于参考的翻译评估之外，我们引入五项用于评估文化适配的标准，这些标准改编自既有的跨文化适配方法。在所选的 LLMs 和语言上，ReciLex 将平均 BLEU 从 13.57 提高到 14.51，将 chrF 从 37.89 提高到 38.74，同时将 TER 从 77.14 降低到 75.12。人工评估进一步显示，在五分量表上，五项文化适配评估标准的提升幅度为 0.11 至 0.36 分。总体而言，我们的工作为研究低资源环境下的文化适配食谱翻译提供了新资源、评估标准和实证评估。

papers.title: StitchRAG: Constructing Compact and Evidence-Preserving Contexts for RAG with Diffusion-Based Stitching
papers.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves factuality by grounding large language models (LLMs) in external evidence. However, long retrieved contexts incur computational overhead and can even hurt performance due to noisy or irrelevant content. We propose \textsc{StitchRAG}, a framework for constructing compact context in RAG. \textsc{StitchRAG} builds a faithful, information-dense context while dynamically compressing the retrieved passages. We adapt the size reduction ratio to each passage by formulating a utility maximization trading-off the retained information and computation costs. We then extract answer candidates and query-related keywords from passages as anchors and collect passage sentences containing anchors under the derived size constraint. Finally, we connect or stitch the collected sentences together using text diffusion to form a coherent and natural context. Experiments on five open-domain QA benchmarks show that \textsc{StitchRAG} consistently outperforms diverse multi-step and compression baselines. Extensive ablations show the effectiveness of dynamic size allocation, anchor preservation, and diffusion-based stitching.
papers.title_zh: StitchRAG：通过基于扩散的拼接为 RAG 构建紧凑且保留证据的上下文
papers.abstract_zh: 检索增强生成（RAG）通过将大型语言模型（LLMs）建立在外部证据之上来提高事实性。然而，长检索上下文会带来计算开销，并且由于存在噪声或无关内容，甚至可能损害性能。我们提出 \textsc{StitchRAG}，一个用于在 RAG 中构建紧凑上下文的框架。\textsc{StitchRAG} 在动态压缩检索到的段落的同时，构建一个忠实且信息密集的上下文。我们通过构建一个在保留信息与计算成本之间进行权衡的效用最大化问题，为每个段落自适应调整尺寸缩减比例。然后，我们从段落中抽取答案候选和与查询相关的关键词作为锚点，并在推导出的尺寸约束下收集包含锚点的段落句子。最后，我们使用文本扩散将收集到的句子连接或拼接在一起，以形成连贯且自然的上下文。在五个开放域问答基准上的实验表明，\textsc{StitchRAG} 始终优于多样的多步与压缩基线。大量消融实验表明动态尺寸分配、锚点保留和基于扩散的拼接的有效性。

papers.title: Compact and Decodable Electrocardiogram Text for Large Language Models
papers.summary: When a twelve-lead electrocardiogram is written as text for a large language model, the number of tokens has to be balanced against the information lost through compression. This paper presents a deterministic encoding that writes eight independent leads as amplitude letters and exact time gaps and recovers the remaining four limb leads algebraically. The key points are selected with a cardiac-cycle-dependent tolerance, the amplitudes are parameterized by a 26-letter logarithmic codebook learned from a training set, and a 10-step tolerance schedule keeps all records within a fixed token budget. The encoding was applied to 21,388 records from the public PTB-XL database and evaluated using an exact decode-and-re-encode round trip, waveform reconstruction error, and a paired comparison of convolutional classifiers trained with 5 different seeds on signals from the original and decoded databases. All records were contained in 4,080 tokens (average: 2,866 tokens, 64.3% fewer than a per-sample transcription), and all stored lead strings were exactly reproduced. The average correlation between the decoded and reference signals was 0.982. The macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.9167 for the reference signals and 0.9157 for the decoded signals (paired difference -0.0010; 95% patient-level bootstrap interval, -0.0028 to 0.0007), within the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -0.010; this is not a confirmatory result, because the test fold had been used during encoder development. The diagnostic content of a compact text can therefore be preserved, while the language model's ability to read the text is yet another matter.
papers.title_zh: 面向大语言模型的紧凑且可解码的心电图文本
papers.abstract_zh: 当把十二导联心电图写成供大语言模型使用的文本时，必须在 token 数量与压缩过程中丢失的信息之间取得平衡。本文提出一种确定性编码：它将八个独立导联写成振幅字母和精确时间间隔，并通过代数方法恢复其余四个肢体导联。关键点依据随心动周期变化的容差进行选择，振幅由从训练集学习得到的 26 字母对数码本参数化，并且 10 步容差调度使所有记录都保持在固定 token 预算之内。该编码被应用于来自公开 PTB-XL 数据库的 21,388 条记录，并使用精确的解码再编码往返、波形重建误差，以及在原始数据库和解码数据库的信号上以 5 个不同随机种子训练的卷积分类器的配对比较进行评估。所有记录都被包含在 4,080 个 token 内（平均：2,866 个 token，比逐样本转录少 64.3%），并且所有存储的导联字符串都被精确复现。解码信号与参考信号之间的平均相关性为 0.982。参考信号的受试者工作特征曲线下面积的宏平均值为 0.9167，解码信号为 0.9157（配对差值 -0.0010；95% 患者水平 bootstrap 区间，-0.0028 至 0.0007），处于预先设定的 -0.010 非劣效性界值之内；这不是一项确证性结果，因为测试折在编码器开发期间已被使用。因此，紧凑文本的诊断内容可以得以保留，而语言模型读取该文本的能力则是另一回事。

papers.title: When Passing Checks Do Not Establish Completion: Evidence Interpretation in Coding Agents
papers.summary: Verification procedures in coding agents must preserve execution facts, interpret their scope and discharge checking obligations. We study these responsibilities through qualified repository checks, controlled evidence consumers and executable workflows. A prospective thirteen-task factorial study finds that correct reported facts need not yield the requested finite verdict. Conversely, all 122 delivered labels in a held-out receipt-supply study are correct, while sixteen responses misreport facts and eleven others exceed authorized scope. Production repair supplies successful controls and finite-supported preservation failures. Across 118 repair episodes on 31 tasks, source interventions separate startup reachability from repair and witness production from the claimed operation. Lifetime and resource controls delimit what passing validation establishes. Generated-note comparisons yield local repair differences but can state false explanations; strong ordinary baselines, new tasks and Skill-transfer studies supply no consistent overall advantage. These results characterize evidence interpretation, applicability and fulfilled actions while limiting claims of general diagnostic superiority, Skill deterioration or deployed folding effects.

papers.title: When Do Typed Decision Models Work in Transportation? Evidence from Travel Choice and Traffic Signal Control
papers.summary: Typed decision models combine natural-language understanding with a structured interface that returns a selected action and an option-level probability distribution without generating lengthy textual responses. Their low inference cost and response latency make them attractive for transportation problems with predefined alternatives. This paper investigates their effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency in two representative transportation tasks: individual travel-mode choice prediction and sequential traffic signal control. We systematically evaluate TypeSafe Jev and GPT-6 Luna Decisions against conventional transportation methods, reinforcement learning algorithms, and four chat-based large language models. Experiments on the Swissmetro dataset show that typed decision models achieve lower prediction accuracy than traditional discrete choice models and the strongest chat-based baseline, while their performance varies substantially with input representation and question framing. In closed-loop traffic signal control experiments, typed decision models demonstrate competitive performance against established controllers in several scenarios, but exhibit performance degradation under more challenging network conditions. Furthermore, the typed models achieve lower inference latency and computational cost than the evaluated chat-based large language models, highlighting their potential for efficient, zero-shot transportation decision-making. Overall, these findings demonstrate both the potential and limitations of typed decision models, emphasizing the importance of input design, task characteristics, and robustness evaluation for their effective application in transportation systems.
papers.title_zh: 类型化决策模型何时在交通运输中有效？来自出行选择与交通信号控制的证据
papers.abstract_zh: 类型化决策模型将自然语言理解与一个结构化接口相结合，该接口返回一个选定的动作以及一个选项层面的概率分布，而不生成冗长的文本回复。其低推理成本与响应延迟使其对具有预定义备选项的交通问题颇具吸引力。本文研究其在两个代表性交通任务中的有效性、鲁棒性与效率：个体出行方式选择预测与序贯交通信号控制。我们系统地将 TypeSafe Jev 与 GPT-6 Luna Decisions 同传统交通方法、强化学习算法以及四种基于对话的大语言模型进行对比评估。在 Swissmetro 数据集上的实验表明，类型化决策模型的预测准确率低于传统离散选择模型以及最强的基于对话的基线，同时其性能会随输入表示与问题表述方式的不同而显著变化。在闭环交通信号控制实验中，类型化决策模型在若干场景下相对于已有控制器展现出有竞争力的性能，但在更具挑战性的路网条件下出现性能下降。此外，与所评估的基于对话的大语言模型相比，类型化模型实现了更低的推理延迟与计算成本，凸显了其在高效、零样本交通决策方面的潜力。总体而言，这些发现既展示了类型化决策模型的潜力，也揭示了其局限性，强调了输入设计、任务特征与鲁棒性评估对于其在交通系统中有效应用的重要性。

papers.title: The Shared Word: Evaluating Language Models on Dutch Word Puzzles
papers.summary: Many LLM benchmarks for languages other than English are translated, multiple-choice, or difficult to score automatically. We introduce The Shared Word (TSW-NL), a Dutch benchmark built around four core principles: it is language-specific, open-vocabulary, human-curated, and deterministically scored. Each puzzle gives three clues that describe different senses or uses of the same Dutch word. The clues are individually ambiguous, requiring the solver to combine evidence across multiple clues. We construct the benchmark from Dutch Wikipedia disambiguation pages, followed by automatic filtering and extensive manual curation. The final dataset contains 222 instances, with three independent human answers per test item. The task is clearly challenging: scores in our human study range from 49.5% to 61.0% and the highest-scoring open-weight model we tested reaches only 39.3%. Many others even score below 20%. At the same time, closed-source models show great progress: GPT-4.1 (April 2025) scores 59.2%, whereas GPT-5.6 Sol with max reasoning scores 88.8%. We believe this task provides a useful addition to Dutch model evaluation, plus a clear recipe that can be applied to construct a similar benchmark for other languages.

papers.title: Can Decision Models Replace LLMs in Real-World Contact Center Classification and Judging Tasks?
papers.summary: Contact center systems often need to make bounded decisions, such as identifying a caller's intent, retrieving the knowledge-base article that answers a query, assessing agent compliance, or judging the output of AI models used in production. Decision models return a typed answer and its probability directly, making them a promising cost-effective alternative to generative Large Language Models (LLMs) in such bounded conversational tasks. However, their effectiveness in real-world contact center applications remains unclear. In this paper, we compare nine decision models against thirteen generative LLMs in zero-shot settings across eight contact center use cases: six classification tasks and two judging tasks. Our experiments demonstrate that many decision models can match the performance of frontier LLMs on contact center classification, and API-based closed decision models achieve this at the lowest per-request cost among the API models we evaluate. We further observe that their confident predictions are more accurate, enabling selective routing in real-world production scenarios. Across classification tasks, the main weakness of most decision models is abstention: they rarely choose the no-answer option, which accounts for most of their gap to the strongest LLMs (although Gemini-Decision-1 is the notable exception in this regard). We also find that the judging quality of decision models drops sharply for smaller models, and they are also more prone to position bias. In short, our findings provide practical guidance for selecting decision models based on abstention behavior, confidence, and deployment cost, rather than overall accuracy alone.
papers.title_zh: 决策模型能否在真实世界的联络中心分类与评判任务中取代LLM？
papers.abstract_zh: 联络中心系统经常需要做出有界决策，例如识别来电者的意图、检索能够回答查询的知识库文章、评估坐席的合规性，或评判生产环境中使用的AI模型的输出。决策模型直接返回一个带类型的答案及其概率，这使其在此类有界对话任务中成为生成式大型语言模型（LLMs）的一种有前景且具有成本效益的替代方案。然而，它们在真实世界联络中心应用中的有效性仍不明确。在本文中，我们在零样本设置下，针对八个联络中心用例——六个分类任务和两个评判任务——将九个决策模型与十三个生成式LLM进行比较。我们的实验表明，许多决策模型在联络中心分类任务上能够达到前沿LLM的性能，而基于API的闭源决策模型在我们评估的API模型中能以最低的每次请求成本实现这一点。我们进一步观察到，它们高置信度的预测更为准确，从而能够在真实世界的生产场景中实现选择性路由。在分类任务中，大多数决策模型的主要弱点是弃权：它们很少选择“无答案”选项，这构成了它们与最强LLM之间差距的大部分（尽管Gemini-Decision-1在这方面是显著的例外）。我们还发现，决策模型的评判质量在较小模型上急剧下降，而且它们也更容易受到位置偏差的影响。简而言之，我们的发现为基于弃权行为、置信度和部署成本而非仅基于总体准确率来选择决策模型提供了实用指导。

papers.title: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science
papers.summary: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) in late 2022 has raised questions about the future of science, but assessing their impact requires understanding how scientific practices were already evolving. We analyze 2.5 million full-text papers across five disciplines from 2015 to 2025, tracing trends over a broad spectrum of lexical, structural, epistemological, and social dimensions. Aside from frequency shifts in some words, most pre-2023 trends continued with limited detectable breaks. Among the notable exceptions, growth in computer science coauthor teams accelerated significantly in Asia, while apparent declines in biomedical topic diversity largely reflected standardization in article formats. Our study establishes an empirical foundation for monitoring the health of global science as LLM adoption deepens.
papers.title_zh: 大型语言模型尚未改变科学
papers.abstract_zh: 2022年末大型语言模型（LLMs）的出现引发了关于科学未来的诸多疑问，但评估其影响需要理解科学实践此前已经在如何演变。我们分析了2015年至2025年间五个学科的250万篇全文论文，追踪了在词汇、结构、认识论和社会等多个维度上的广泛趋势。除了某些词语的频率变化之外，2023年之前的大部分趋势仍在延续，可检测到的中断有限。在值得注意的例外中，计算机科学领域合著者团队的增长在亚洲显著加速，而生物医学主题多样性表面上的下降在很大程度上反映了文章格式的标准化。我们的研究为在LLM应用不断深化之际监测全球科学的健康状况奠定了实证基础。

papers.title: TPHC: Improving Hyper-Connections with Tensor-Parallel Grouped Updates
papers.summary: Hyper-Connections (HC) expand the residual stream of a Transformer into $N$ parallel streams, and manifold-constrained HC (mHC) stabilizes them at scale. However, mHC benefits little from more than four streams, partly because each sublayer writes a single output to all streams, limiting how differently they can be updated. In this work, we propose TPHC, which integrates tensor-parallel (TP) shards with HC streams to promote greater independence across streams. Specifically, we route a separate mixture of the residual streams to each TP shard and keep the individual shard outputs separate during write-back, so each stream can receive a different mixture of those outputs. This design makes the residual-stream updates more expressive without adding parameters or FLOPs to the attention or FFN sublayers. With native support for stream sharding under TP, TPHC requires only 9% more training time than mHC on an 8B model when both use four streams. Increasing the number of streams from four to sixteen raises its training time by only 19%. On a 1.1B model trained on 100B tokens, TPHC reduces validation loss by 0.7-1.0% and raises average zero-shot accuracy across six commonsense reasoning benchmarks by 0.3-0.7 percentage points relative to mHC at matched stream counts $N\in\{4,8,16\}$. Our code is available at https://github.com/wuyou2002/TPHC.

papers.title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
papers.summary: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable. We introduce the VFM, a tree-attention verifier that encodes the shared context and target text, and scores N natural language criteria in parallel, returning independent per-criterion ternary verdicts. The VFM is pretrained on CriteriaBank, a corpus of 394K (context, target, criterion, verdict) tuples spanning over 321K distinct criterion strings. A finetuned VFM-4B outperforms GPT-5.4 on a synthetic governance benchmark. On the DynaBench multi-criterion benchmark, it outperforms DynaGuard-4B on trace-level failure detection, and its per-criterion verdicts localize the violated rule and support focused escalation to a larger chain-of-thought judge. We show that CriteriaBank pretraining improves cross-domain transfer, particularly in the low-data regime, while matching a strong direct-finetuning control at full data. On a single H100, VFM-4B evaluates 1,000 criteria against a 4K-token context in under 2s at <11 GB VRAM, making it suitable for runtime verification.

papers.title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language
papers.summary: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce tree-grams, autoregressive generative $n$-gram models that build the conditional probability tensor $p(x_n \mid x_{1:n-1})$ through a hierarchical composition of order-2 and order-3 tensors. $n$ controls the maximal context window, whereas a rank hyperparameter $d$ controls model capacity, yielding an interpretable and systematically scalable family of approximators of language. We show how tree-grams outperform existing $n$-gram baselines, while remaining competitive with deep transformer-based language models. We demonstrate the utility of such controlled approximations by using tree-grams as generative models. In particular, we show that hyperparameter transfer under $μ$P can be made more robust when narrower models are tuned on simpler data, generated by tree-grams with moderate $n$ and $d$. In addition, we show that entropy and effective range of correlations control performance gap after fine-tuning. This is because tree-grams allow us to explicitly control horizon and capacity. When allowed to route across candidate topologies, we observe emergent sparsity in tree-grams. Such concentrated routing permits pruning upto 95\% of topologies without significant change in performance.

papers.title: Natural Language Programming: Rethinking Language, Memory, and Cognition in the Era of Generative AI
papers.summary: Generative Artificial Intelligence is transforming the role of natural language in computational systems. In classical Natural Language Processing (NLP), language was treated as an object of computation: something to analyse, classify, translate, or generate. Large Language Models (LLMs) challenge this perspective, enabling natural language to function increasingly as an executable cognitive medium through which humans structure reasoning, orchestrate problem solving, and regulate hybrid human/AI workflows. This paper introduces Natural Language Programming (NLPg) as a theoretical and epistemological extension of traditional NLP. Rather than focusing on language understanding alone, NLPg conceptualises prompts as dynamic cognitive artefacts that externalise goals, constraints, assumptions, validation criteria, and intermediate reasoning states. Prompting is thus not merely a technical interaction technique, but a form of dialogic cognitive programming operating within distributed human/AI memory architectures. Building on theories of distributed cognition, extended mind, metacognition, and dialogic learning, the paper proposes the notion of Dialogic Working Memory, describing how prompts and conversational states function as temporary external memory structures supporting reasoning continuity and reflective regulation. We further map existing memory architectures (BTMA, SKGE, RMR) onto this framework, illustrating how episodic, semantic, and metacognitive layers support long-horizon conversational coherence. Finally, implications for computational linguistics and AI/mediated knowledge systems are discussed, suggesting a post symbolic and post interface paradigm in which natural language operates simultaneously as communication medium, executable specification, cognitive scaffold, and distributed memory architecture.
papers.title_zh: 自然语言编程：生成式人工智能时代对语言、记忆与认知的再思考
papers.abstract_zh: 生成式人工智能正在改变自然语言在计算系统中的作用。在经典自然语言处理（NLP）中，语言被视为计算的对象：一种可供分析、分类、翻译或生成的东西。大语言模型（LLMs）挑战了这一观点，使自然语言日益发挥可执行认知媒介的功能，人类通过它来组织推理、编排问题求解并调节人类/人工智能混合工作流。本文引入自然语言编程（NLPg），作为传统NLP在理论和认识论上的扩展。NLPg并非仅关注语言理解，而是将提示概念化为动态认知人工物，它们外化目标、约束、假设、验证标准以及中间推理状态。因此，提示不仅是一种技术性交互技巧，而且是一种在分布式人类/人工智能记忆架构内运行的对话式认知编程形式。基于分布式认知、延展心智、元认知和对话式学习等理论，本文提出对话式工作记忆的概念，描述提示和对话状态如何作为临时外部记忆结构发挥作用，支持推理连续性和反思性调节。我们进一步将现有记忆架构（BTMA、SKGE、RMR）映射到该框架中，说明情景层、语义层和元认知层如何支持长时程对话连贯性。最后，讨论了其对计算语言学和人工智能/中介化知识系统的启示，提出一种后符号与后界面范式，其中自然语言同时作为传播媒介、可执行规范、认知支架和分布式记忆架构运行。

papers.title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue
papers.summary: Effective multi-agent collaboration requires agents to adapt task allocation as goals and responsibilities evolve. Prior task-allocation frameworks often assume static goals, full observability, or rely on large language models (LLMs) without explicit, verifiable beliefs about task allocation or intent. These assumptions limit their applicability to real-world collaboration, where agents often lack full information about each other's actions, progress, or local environment. To support dynamic task allocation under partial observability, we introduce a communication-augmented Bayesian task-allocation framework. Our agent uses dialogue to reduce uncertainty about the environment and collaborators, while keeping decisions grounded in explicit probabilistic beliefs. We evaluate our framework in an Overcooked domain extended with dynamically arriving tasks under both full and partial object-space observability. Our communication agent consistently outperforms a vanilla LLM agent in both settings. Additionally, our framework performs comparably to a non-communicating task-allocation baseline under full observability, but substantially outperforms it under partial observability as task complexity increases by an average speed up of 0.585 and completes on average 18 timesteps faster. These results indicate that our agent is more efficient in dynamic task allocation than baselines in partially observable environments, and that communication is important as available information decreases.
papers.title_zh: 基于对话的动态任务分配
papers.abstract_zh: 有效的多智能体协作要求智能体在目标和职责演变时调整任务分配。先前的任务分配框架通常假设目标是静态的、具有完全可观测性，或者依赖大语言模型（LLMs）而没有关于任务分配或意图的显式、可验证的信念。这些假设限制了它们对现实世界协作的适用性，在现实世界协作中，智能体通常缺乏关于彼此行动、进度或局部环境的完整信息。为了在部分可观测性下支持动态任务分配，我们引入了一个通信增强的贝叶斯任务分配框架。我们的智能体利用对话来降低关于环境和协作者的不确定性，同时使决策建立在显式的概率信念之上。我们在一个 Overcooked 领域中对我们的框架进行评估，该领域在完全和部分对象空间可观测性下都扩展了动态到达的任务。我们的通信智能体在两种设置中始终优于普通 LLM 智能体。此外，我们的框架在完全可观测性下与一个非通信的任务分配基线表现相当，但在部分可观测性下随着任务复杂度增加而显著优于它，平均加速 0.585，并平均快 18 个时间步完成。这些结果表明，在部分可观测环境中，我们的智能体在动态任务分配上比基线更高效，并且随着可用信息减少，通信是重要的。

papers.title: MoE--LoRA Methods for Multilingual Adaptation: A Systematic Empirical Study
papers.summary: Routed low-rank adapters offer a parameter-efficient means to improve the performance of large language models (LLMs) across tasks. Hence, it is assumed that they can also be used to improve the support of low-resource languages in LLMs, which currently serve English far better than the thousands of other languages spoken worldwide. However, this assumption has never been verified empirically under a shared multilingual evaluation protocol. We address exactly this gap by comparing eight low-rank adaptation (LoRA) methods on a frozen base model using 200 unique languages in more than 9{,}000 evaluation settings. Our results suggest that a reduced-scale search can identify viable configurations of LoRA methods but does not reliably predict their relative performance, as the top-ranking configuration is never best at scale. LoRA reliably improves language-model fit on translation data, consistently degrades reading comprehension, and benefits low-resource languages most. These findings suggest that LoRA methods should be regarded as targeted tools rather than general-purpose means for improving the multilingual capabilities of LLMs.
papers.title_zh: 面向多语言适配的 MoE--LoRA 方法：一项系统性的实证研究
papers.abstract_zh: 路由低秩适配器提供了一种参数高效的方法，用于提升大语言模型（LLMs）在各类任务上的性能。因此，人们假设它们也可用于改善 LLMs 对低资源语言的支持，而目前 LLMs 对英语的服务远好于对全球使用的数千种其他语言的服务。然而，这一假设从未在共享的多语言评估协议下得到实证验证。我们正是通过在一个冻结的基础模型上比较八种低秩适配（LoRA）方法，在超过 9{,}000 个评估设置中使用 200 种独特语言，来弥补这一空白。我们的结果表明，缩小规模的搜索可以识别出 LoRA 方法的可行配置，但不能可靠预测它们的相对性能，因为排名最高的配置在规模扩大后从来不是最佳的。LoRA 可靠地改善了翻译数据上的语言模型拟合，持续使阅读理解性能下降，并且对低资源语言最有益。这些发现表明，LoRA 方法应被视为有针对性的工具，而不是提升 LLMs 多语言能力的通用手段。

papers.title: Polarity Composition Hypothesis: Causal Evidence from Negation in NLI
papers.summary: We investigate how language models process negation in natural language inference (NLI). We propose the \textit{Polarity Composition Hypothesis}, a high-level causal model of this computation. Behavioral evaluations show that language-model predictions largely conform to the proposed hypothesis. Using Distributed Alignment Search, we identify causally effective subspaces aligned with the variables in the polarity-composition hypothesis. These representations transfer across negation forms and partially to a subset of MNLI. We release the dataset and code.

papers.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining
papers.summary: Next-token prediction is relied upon to learn both predictive behavior and internal representations. We ask whether representation structure itself should be an explicit inductive bias. Motivated by the two-part coding view of Kolmogorov complexity, we study a structure--residual principle in which a representation separates structure from realization detail. We instantiate this principle in two complementary ways. Boundary Bottleneck Concept (BBC) routes information from token segments through boundary carriers while preserving local autoregressive computation. Continuous Concept (CC) regularizes representation geometry and induces a spectral decomposition into low-frequency structure and high-frequency residual. We derive coding bounds for both views and show that multiplicity-corrected boundary attention becomes exact as the within-segment path energy vanishes. Empirically, BBC and CC exhibit strikingly different depth preferences: BBC works best in early layers, whereas CC is most effective in later layers. At 300M training tokens, combining BBC and CC improves NLL by 1.44\% on GPT-2 Medium. These gains persist with training runs up to 20B tokens. Representation diagnostics show that BBC increases the relative predictive importance of boundary states, while CC reduces spectral residual energy. Together, these results suggest that structure--residual biases can improve language-model pretraining beyond next-token prediction. Code: https://github.com/haihuang-ml/structure-residual

papers.title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
papers.summary: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $φ= 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any of them, and no method in this family performs an experiment that could. The substantive claims fail independently: bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated. Its complement, scored on the opposite label, reliably destroys refusal behaviour ($p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$), demonstrating that the pipeline detects effects at this scale.
papers.title_zh: 偏见头究竟度量了什么？头级别偏见归因中的不可识别性
papers.abstract_zh: 将大语言模型中的社会偏见定位到单个注意力头、并通过消融将其移除的方法，其有效性是由其对某个公平性指标的影响来验证的，而从未由证据表明选择这些头的统计量度量的是偏见。我们在 Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct 和 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 上对此进行审计。头图谱与一个标签盲的回复长度图谱的相关性分别为 $\rho= -0.950$ 和 $-0.768$，这似乎指认出一个表层混淆因素。一个打破长度—标签耦合的干预否定了这一解读：在提示保持固定的情况下，回复长度只解释该统计量方差的 1%。真正能解释它的是提示同一性，占方差的 64%，其排序并不随长度单调变化。在任何固定提示内部，公平性标签、回复长度以及受保护群体标记的出现三者共线，$\phi= 0.95$，部分上是由于标注规则的定义所致，因此任何观察性分析都无法将该图谱归因于其中任何一个，而这一族方法中也没有任何一种执行了能够做到这一点的实验。实质性主张各自独立地失败：在两种参照解读下，偏见选择性在两个模型上都不是集中于后层，并且我们测试的任何头集合在被消融时都不能降低不公平率。其补集在相反标签上评分时，能够可靠地破坏拒答行为（$p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$），这表明该流程能够检测到这一量级的效应。

papers.title: LLMs as Validators for Cross-Chain Bridges: Evaluating Source-Level and Transaction-Level Attack Detection on Solana
papers.summary: Cross-chain bridges have suffered substantial asset losses due to vulnerabilities in their on-chain programs. On Solana, missing validation checks can enable exploits even when the underlying blockchain operates correctly. The ability of large language models (LLMs) to diagnose these flaws from source code or transaction records, rather than merely raise alarms, remains insufficiently understood. We implement a native Rust lock-and-mint bridge on a local Solana validator with four exploitable variants: two model flaws from the Cashio and Wormhole incidents, while the other two represent vulnerability classes documented in Solana security audits. Paired vulnerable and secure programs, together with successful attacks, benign sessions, and blocked attempts, allow us to distinguish correct diagnoses from unsupported alarms. We evaluate six configurations of five open-weight models across 16,800 responses, compare source inputs with and without comments, and grade 7,200 answers on vulnerable inputs using two blinded LLM graders. The results reveal substantial differences across conditions: without comments, models diagnose 24% of vulnerable source inputs while frequently flagging the secure bridge. Transaction diagnosis is high for the missing-signer scenario but averages 6% across the other three scenarios. Original comments, some of which describe the flaw, increase source diagnosis to 60%. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing correct vulnerability diagnoses from unsupported alarms in bridge security review.
papers.title_zh: 大型语言模型作为跨链桥的验证器：评估Solana上的源代码级与交易级攻击检测
papers.abstract_zh: 跨链桥因其链上程序中的漏洞而遭受了大量资产损失。在Solana上，即使底层区块链正常运行，缺失的验证检查也可能使漏洞被利用。大型语言模型（LLM）能否从源代码或交易记录中诊断这些缺陷，而不仅仅是发出告警，目前仍缺乏足够认识。我们在本地Solana验证器上实现了一个原生Rust锁定-铸造桥，并包含四个可利用变体：其中两个是来自Cashio和Wormhole事件的建模缺陷，而另外两个代表Solana安全审计中记录过的漏洞类别。成对的易受攻击程序与安全程序，连同成功攻击、良性会话和被阻止的尝试，使我们能够区分正确诊断与无依据告警。我们评估了五个开放权重模型的六种配置在16,800条响应上的表现，比较了带注释与不带注释的源代码输入，并使用两名盲评LLM评分者对易受攻击输入上的7,200个回答进行评分。结果揭示了不同条件之间的显著差异：在不带注释时，模型诊断出24%的易受攻击源代码输入，同时频繁将安全桥标记为有问题。交易诊断在缺失签名者场景中较高，但在其他三个场景中平均仅为6%。原始注释——其中一些描述了该缺陷——将源代码诊断率提高到60%。这些发现凸显了在桥安全审查中区分正确漏洞诊断与无依据告警的重要性。

papers.title: Threat Landscape of Vibe Coding and the Road to Secure Autonomy
papers.summary: Vibe coding is reshaping software development, enabling faster implementation and allowing individuals with limited programming experience to describe requirements in natural language while AI agents write, test, and deploy the code. As these agents evolve into autonomous systems that execute commands, manage dependencies, access cloud resources, and interact with other agents, their security risks extend beyond incorrect code to actions with direct consequences for software systems. Although research on these risks is expanding, it remains fragmented across areas including prompt injection, insecure code generation, supply-chain attacks, and human factors, with limited consensus on terminology, threat assumptions, and evaluation. This paper consolidates emerging research through the lens of the vibe coding workflow. We establish a reference architecture, characterise six levels of agent autonomy, and develop a threat model centred on five trust boundaries spanning developers, AI models, tools, cloud infrastructure, and the wider software ecosystem. Building on this foundation, we propose a taxonomy of twenty-one threats across nine classes. For each threat, we review the available evidence, assess proposed defences, and identify limitations. Our analysis highlights that risks increase with agents' operational authority, while most defences rely on model judgement and address isolated threats. Finally, we identify eleven research challenges, including enforceable limits on agent authority and shared benchmarks and methodologies for assessing vibe coding security.

papers.title: Bajillion: Cryptographic Clearing for Micropayments
papers.summary: Much of the web is funded by advertising, a model that erodes as humans delegate browsing to AI agents acting on their behalf. A natural replacement is for agents to pay for what they consume, often a fraction of a cent per request. At the scale of web traffic, this could mean tens or even hundreds of millions of payments per second. We present Bajillion, a clearing protocol for scalable micropayments. A sender signs a payment request, and an untrusted operator answers with a preconfirmation, which promises the receiver that it will be paid. Periodically, the operator closes an epoch by posting only the net effect of its payments on chain. Bajillion guarantees that a malicious operator can only omit payments -- it can never debit a sender beyond what it signed, nor misdirect a transfer. Posted balances are therefore finalized immediately and can be withdrawn. By design, senders never have to raise disputes, making it suitable for ephemeral AI agents. A receiver that is shortchanged can prove that a close omitted a preconfirmed payment, which halts the protocol and lets every user exit with its finalized balance. Requests from different senders can be processed independently, allowing the operator to parallelize up to the number of senders. We capture these guarantees in an ideal functionality for accountable clearing and prove that Bajillion realizes it.

papers.title: A Forensic Analysis of Metadata and Information Leakage in Swedish Public Documents
papers.summary: This study investigates metadata and structural content leakage in publicly available PDF documents from 30 Swedish public-sector authorities. Using an automated collection pipeline and ExifTool-based extraction, 2,876 documents were analyzed and classified using an R0-R3 risk taxonomy. Results reveal that 48.4% of documents exhibit significant metadata exposure (R2 or R3), with significant variation across institutional tiers (p < 0.001). Longitudinal analysis across three legislative periods reveals a statistically significant reduction in metadata exposure between the baseline and post-enactment periods, yet 44.9% of documents published after the enactment of the Swedish Cybersäkerhetslagen continue to leak sensitive metadata. Furthermore, 41.6% of documents contain incremental update layers; forensic analysis recovered verifiable text alterations, including deleted personal data and internal identifiers, from 228 of these cases. These findings highlight persistent regulatory lag and a systemic reliance on default, unsanitized document publication workflows within the Swedish public sector.

papers.title: CNN Architecture Comparison for Malware Classification with Limited Training Data
papers.summary: Traditional malware classification methods struggle to keep pace with rapidly evolving threats. Image-based malware classification offers a promising alternative by converting malware binaries into grayscale images for analysis with deep learning. While effective, organizations often face practical constraints in acquiring sufficient training data, especially for newer threats. This thesis investigates dual-path CNN architectures with intermediate feature fusion as a potential enhancement for malware classification, with particular focus on how varying training data size affects their comparative performance against traditional single-path approaches. This research implements and compares two models: a baseline single-path using the pre-trained VGG16 architecture and a dual-path model that combines VGG16 with a custom CNN through intermediate feature fusion. Both architectures are evaluated on a binary classification task distinguishing between two malware families (C2Lop.P trojan and Dialplatform.B worm) from the Malimg dataset. Each model is trained across four different training data proportions (20%, 40%, 60%, and 80%), with three training runs per size to ensure statistical robustness, while being evaluated on complementary test sets of varying sizes. Though both architectures achieved perfect classification performance across all training percentages, the study revealed significant differences in secondary metrics including training efficiency, robustness to noise perturbation, and architectural complexity. The findings challenge common assumptions about complex architectures, demonstrating that simpler models can offer superior efficiency and robustness without sacrificing classification performance in image-based malware analysis.

papers.title: PersonaHate: A Scalable Persona-Based Data Synthesis Pipeline for Hate Speech Analysis
papers.summary: Hate speech remains a persistent and evolving threat on online platforms. The widespread use of large language models (LLMs) further intensifies this problem by making hateful content easier and cheaper to generate at scale. Although stronger hate speech detectors continue to be proposed, their performance remains uneven across target identity groups and different forms of hateful expression, partly because existing training data provides only limited coverage of these cases. Thus, we introduce PersonaHate, a scalable persona-driven data synthesis pipeline for constructing diverse hate speech datasets. PersonaHate begins with a large persona pool of 457K personas drawn from two real-world sources. Conditioned on selected personas from this pool, it prompts eight LLMs to generate hate speech across 34 identity groups and performs multi-judge annotation to obtain reliable labels. The resulting corpus contains 791K samples, from which we curate a 67K group-balanced training set. Our modular design also supports extension to new identity groups, generators, and emerging hate targets. Built upon this dataset, we evaluate two detector training strategies: training from scratch and further fine-tuning. Results show that all trained models achieve competitive performance across four widely used external benchmarks. Notably, a 184M-parameter DeBERTa-v3 model trained on PersonaHate reaches 77.5% average F1 and 79.4% average accuracy, outperforming OpenAI's Moderation API on HateBenchSet and MHS. Furthermore, fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B raises its average F1 from 70.7% to 78.4%, a gain of 7.7 percentage points, surpassing LlamaGuard-3, Meta's official safety model based on the same Llama-3.1-8B architecture, on three of four benchmarks. These results show that PersonaHate can substantially improve the robustness and cross-dataset generalization of hate speech detectors.
papers.title_zh: PersonaHate：一种用于仇恨言论分析的可扩展的基于人物画像的数据合成流水线
papers.abstract_zh: 仇恨言论仍然是在线平台上一种持续存在且不断演变的威胁。大型语言模型（LLMs）的广泛使用通过使仇恨内容更容易、更便宜地大规模生成，进一步加剧了这一问题。尽管不断有更强的仇恨言论检测器被提出，但它们在目标身份群体和不同形式的仇恨表达上的表现仍然不均衡，部分原因是现有训练数据对这些情况的覆盖有限。因此，我们提出 PersonaHate，一种可扩展的、由人物画像驱动的数据合成流水线，用于构建多样化的仇恨言论数据集。PersonaHate 从包含 457K 个人物画像的大型人物画像池开始，这些画像取自两个真实世界来源。以从该池中选择的人物画像为条件，它提示八个 LLMs 生成跨越 34 个身份群体的仇恨言论，并执行多评判者标注以获得可靠的标签。得到的语料库包含 791K 个样本，我们从中整理出一个 67K 的群体平衡训练集。我们的模块化设计还支持扩展到新的身份群体、生成器和新兴的仇恨目标。基于该数据集，我们评估了两种检测器训练策略：从头训练和进一步微调。结果表明，所有训练后的模型在四个广泛使用的外部基准上均取得了有竞争力的性能。值得注意的是，一个在 PersonaHate 上训练的 184M 参数 DeBERTa-v3 模型达到 77.5% 的平均 F1 和 79.4% 的平均准确率，在 HateBenchSet 和 MHS 上优于 OpenAI's Moderation API。此外，微调 Llama-3.1-8B 将其平均 F1 从 70.7% 提高到 78.4%，提升了 7.7 个百分点，并在四个基准中的三个上超过了 LlamaGuard-3——Meta 基于相同 Llama-3.1-8B 架构的官方安全模型。这些结果表明，PersonaHate 能够显著提高仇恨言论检测器的鲁棒性和跨数据集泛化能力。

papers.title: Eight in Ten LLMs Leak System-Prompt Secrets: Nevan, an Agentic Capture-the-Flag Study
papers.summary: We audit instruction-hierarchy enforcement across 363 text-in/text-out models from the OpenRouter catalog. The research question we answer with this experiment is which models disclose a protected secret embedded in the system prompt, and through which techniques. Each model guards a secret 16-character flag set in its system prompt, while an artificial intelligence (AI) agent (OpenCode, powered by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), steered by a human researcher, tries to persuade it to emit the flag. The flag was exfiltrated from 296 of the 363 models, plus four models released after the initial catalog freeze, for 300 captures in total. Of these, 170 involved a non-English language pivot, most often French. Each capture shows that a model ranked a user request above its system instruction at least once. It does not show that the model provably resists untested attacks, nor that it would consistently leak semantically sensitive data, nor that it is vulnerable to harmful-content jailbreaks. For practitioners, we draw three lessons: do not store secrets in system prompts, enforce critical behavior outside the model with output validation and deterministic checks, and do not let a large language model (LLM) judge be the sole decider of consequential outcomes.
papers.title_zh: 十分之八的大语言模型泄露系统提示词机密：Nevan，一项智能体式夺旗研究
papers.abstract_zh: 我们审计了 OpenRouter 目录中 363 个文本输入/文本输出模型对指令层级的执行情况。本实验所要回答的研究问题是：哪些模型会泄露嵌入系统提示词中的受保护机密，以及通过哪些技术手段。每个模型守护一个设置在其系统提示词中的 16 字符机密 flag，而一个由人类研究者操控的人工智能（AI）智能体（OpenCode，由 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 驱动）试图说服其输出该 flag。该 flag 从 363 个模型中的 296 个模型，以及初始目录冻结之后发布的四个模型中被成功窃取，总计 300 次捕获。其中，170 次涉及非英语语言转换，最常见的是法语。每一次捕获都表明，某个模型至少有一次将用户请求置于其系统指令之上。这并不表明该模型可被证明能够抵御未经测试的攻击，也不表明它会持续泄露语义敏感数据，也不表明它易受有害内容越狱的影响。对于实践者，我们得出三条教训：不要在系统提示词中存储机密；通过输出验证和确定性检查在模型之外强制执行关键行为；不要让大语言模型（LLM）评判者成为重大后果的唯一决定者。

papers.title: Hierarchical Personalized Federated Learning for Fine-Grained Intrusion Detection: A Multi-Class Analysis in Heterogeneous Attack Environments
papers.summary: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) play a vital role in protecting modern network infrastructures. Although Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training without sharing raw network traffic, global models struggle with non-IID attack distributions. Moreover, practical security operations require fine-grained attack classification for targeted threat responses. To address these challenges, this paper investigates the convergence dynamics and performance of Hierarchical Personalized Federated Learning (HPFL), which combines multi-tier aggregation with client-level personalization, for 8-class, 6-class, and 4-class intrusion detection using Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) models implemented in NVIDIA FLARE on the CICIDS2017 dataset. Experimental results show that personalized HPFL models achieve micro F1-scores up to 0.9911 in the 6-class task, while the overall local accuracy reaches 0.9975 in the 8-class task. On 8-class local test sets, HPFL achieves a micro F1-score of 0.9901 and a macro F1-score of 0.8324, outperforming FedAvg (0.7176) and FedProx (0.5624) in macro F1. Cross-client evaluations demonstrate out-of-distribution generalization, with HPFL achieving a 4-class micro F1-score of 0.9294 compared with 0.9140 for standalone local models. Furthermore, distance-weighted network analysis estimates a 48.9% reduction in transmission overhead compared with conventional FL (194.4 MB vs. 380.3 MB for the 8-class task). These findings demonstrate HPFLs potential as an accurate, privacy-preserving, and communication-efficient approach to fine-grained intrusion detection in heterogeneous networks.

papers.title: Is 4-Bit Quantization More Than Noise to a Chat Model's Safety Behaviour? Attributing Behavioural Shifts with Matched Perturbations
papers.summary: Chat models on phones and laptops are usually 4-bit copies of the model that was evaluated, and audits of such copies disagree about what quantization does to refusal. A 4-bit build is one of many weight perturbations of the same size, so a change in its behaviour could come from its specific rounding error or from any perturbation that large. In a pre-registered study of three 3-4B chat models, with paired tests, blind human labels and an 8-bit null, we find two 4-bit shifts of opposite sign: with a compliant reply prefilled, Qwen2.5-3B continues into harmful content more often, and on held-out jailbreaks Llama-3.2-3B complies 10.3 points less often. Matched perturbations separate the two. Shuffled and Gaussian versions of the error average close to zero, while scaling the real error, from its mirror image to twice its size, changes behaviour near-linearly. At half the real error, Llama's likelihood is almost unchanged, yet it already complies 5.8 points less often, and llama.cpp's Q4_K_M, at the same bits per weight, moves neither model. Refusal under 4-bit quantization depends on the specific rounding error, not on bits per weight or likelihood, so each build has to be compared with its original.

papers.title: GapLeak: When Privacy-Preserving LLM-based Web Agents Become a Privacy Risk
papers.summary: Large Language Model (LLM)-based web agents rely on data minimization and least privilege to protect user privacy. We show that these principles are necessary but insufficient: they constrain authorized sources, but not higher-sensitivity sources that remain reachable. A website can request a field unavailable from authorized sources, creating an information gap. To complete the task, a goal-driven agent may escalate to reachable but unauthorized sources and disclose accumulated sensitive information. We formalize this vulnerability as GapLeak, where an adversary exploits a legitimate web form without prompt injection or other malicious instructions. We evaluate GapLeak on three web-agent frameworks and six LLMs from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI across recruitment, e-commerce, travel, and healthcare. GapLeak induces an average unauthorized disclosure of approximately 37%. The information gap is the primary driver: eliminating it reduces disclosure by more than 50%. Existing instruction-level defenses based on least privilege partially mitigate the vulnerability but often reduce task success. We propose submission-time verification, which filters unauthorized content before form submission, eliminating over 96% of unauthorized disclosures while preserving task success.
papers.title_zh: GapLeak：当隐私保护型基于LLM的Web代理成为隐私风险
papers.abstract_zh: 基于大型语言模型（LLM）的Web代理依赖数据最小化和最小权限来保护用户隐私。我们表明，这些原则必要但不充分：它们约束了授权来源，但并未约束仍然可及的高敏感性来源。一个网站可以请求无法从授权来源获得的字段，从而造成信息缺口。为完成任务，目标驱动的代理可能升级访问，触达可及但未经授权的来源，并泄露已累积的敏感信息。我们将这一漏洞形式化为GapLeak，其中对手无需提示注入或其他恶意指令即可利用合法的Web表单。我们在三个Web代理框架以及来自Anthropic、Google和OpenAI的六个LLM上，在招聘、电子商务、旅行和医疗保健领域评估GapLeak。GapLeak平均引发约37%的未经授权披露。信息缺口是主要驱动因素：消除它可将披露减少50%以上。现有基于最小权限的指令级防御可部分缓解该漏洞，但通常会降低任务成功率。我们提出提交时验证，在表单提交前过滤未经授权的内容，在保持任务成功的同时消除超过96%的未经授权披露。

papers.title: From Token Changes to Task Failures: Bit Flips in a Shared KV-Cache Block
papers.summary: In LLM serving systems with prefix caching, each KV block of a shared system prompt is held in GPU memory as a single physical copy, which every request with that prompt reads. Our earlier work measured change and showed that one bit flip in such a block changes many later responses without making them visibly degenerate. This paper extends that work by measuring how often the changed responses are wrong. Using software fault injection into vLLM serving Qwen3-8B, we flip the most significant mantissa bit or the sign bit of a value in such a block. We score responses on four tasks: code generation, short-answer questions, multiple-choice reasoning, and refusal under a policy. The fraction of changes that turned a correct response wrong depended strongly on the task: 0.023 on MBPP+ and 0.59 on held-out TriviaQA at the mantissa bit, and 0.019 and 0.60 at the sign bit. Harm fell on requests whose sampled answers are sometimes wrong, so the damage of a flip depends on how common such requests are. Harmed responses looked like ordinary errors, so a flip should be detected by checking cached blocks rather than by monitoring outputs.

papers.title: Dressed in Authority: Practical Black-Box Jailbreaking of MLLMs via Visual Trust Bias
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are rapidly advancing, yet their safety remains a critical concern, especially under jailbreak attempts. Existing MLLM jailbreaks either inject fragile adversarial perturbations into irrelevant images or synthesize toxic visual cues to achieve text-driven attack intents. In contrast, a more practical MLLM jailbreak emphasizes enhancing attack efficacy directly on naturally occurring harmful image-text pairs. We address this problem by proposing Visual Trust Bias Attack (VTBA), a new jailbreak framework that exploits a previously overlooked attack surface: MLLMs exhibit an intrinsic trust bias toward authoritative visual features, which enables transferable and stealthy jailbreaks. VTBA constructs a bank of authoritative templates, matches each input pair to the most relevant one, and integrates the harmful intent into the selected layout, thereby leveraging credible visual cues to override safety refusals while preserving naturalness. We further construct a dataset of 2,500 naturally occurring image-text pairs to evaluate jailbreaks in this practical multimodal setting. Extensive experiments show that our method consistently achieves high attack success rates across strong MLLMs, revealing a severe and previously underexplored weakness in current multimodal safety alignment. Warning: This paper may contain sensitive content.
papers.title_zh: 披着权威外衣：通过视觉信任偏差对 MLLM 进行实用的黑盒越狱
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）正在快速发展，但其安全性仍然是一个关键问题，尤其是在越狱尝试下。现有的 MLLM 越狱方法要么向无关图像中注入脆弱的对抗扰动，要么合成有害的视觉线索以实现文本驱动的攻击意图。相比之下，一种更实用的 MLLM 越狱强调直接在自然出现的有害图文对上增强攻击效果。我们通过提出视觉信任偏差攻击（Visual Trust Bias Attack，VTBA）来解决这一问题，这是一种新的越狱框架，利用了一个此前被忽视的攻击面：MLLM 对权威性视觉特征表现出一种内在的信任偏差，这使得可迁移且隐蔽的越狱成为可能。VTBA 构建一个权威模板库，将每个输入图文对匹配到最相关的模板，并将有害意图整合到所选布局中，从而利用可信的视觉线索覆盖安全拒绝，同时保持自然性。我们进一步构建了一个包含 2,500 个自然出现的图文对的数据集，以评估这一实用多模态设置下的越狱。大量实验表明，我们的方法在强 MLLM 上始终实现高攻击成功率，揭示了当前多模态安全对齐中一个严重且此前未被充分探索的弱点。警告：本文可能包含敏感内容。

papers.title: TetherMark: Instance-Level Watermark Authentication Against Cross-Instance Transplantation
papers.summary: Robust watermarking is commonly verified by asking whether a hidden payload remains decodable after compression, geometric distortion, or generative editing. Localized and semantic extensions may additionally check whether an expected region or category is still present. These tests establish evidence validity or content consistency, but not whether the evidence still belongs to the particular visual instance registered by its owner. We expose cross-instance transplantation: an attacker extracts or estimates valid watermark evidence from one registered image and transfers it to a different image of the same category. The message can still decode, the expected content can remain present, and the result can look natural, even though the evidence has been reassigned to the wrong instance. To enable instance-level watermark authentication, we introduce TetherMark, a post-hoc watermark that combines two complementary checks. The message check verifies an edit-robust payload, while the relation check uses secret patch-pair selection, a registered response, natural correspondence transport, and enrollment normalization to test consistency with the registered instance. The verifier accepts only when both checks pass. Across 240 test subjects, TetherMark attains 92.08% legitimate true acceptance with 9.17% and 16.25% attack success under WmForger and WMCopier, respectively, yielding the highest instance-binding balanced accuracy under both attacks.

papers.title: From Attack Tree to Model Checker: Binding CAPEC Patterns to Verify Robotic System Security
papers.summary: Security-minded verification of autonomous and robotic systems presupposes an attacker, yet the path from a threat catalogue to a checkable attacker model is still traversed by hand. This research preview presents the theory and construction of a pipeline that mechanises it. Each leaf of an attack tree is mapped to a CAPEC attack pattern and written in first-order logic as a rule: the attacker's prerequisites imply the attack's effect. Casting the pattern as such a rule is what makes it operational - its variables can be bound to a specific system's parts, and its prerequisites can then be tested against that system under a chosen configuration of security controls. Binding is our means of verifying whether a system is vulnerable to a given attack: from a bound pattern we derive an attacker model, turn its effect into a temporal-logic property, and check that property against the system with and without a countermeasure, reporting the control that defeats the attack. We describe the signature, schemas, profiles for approach, and explore how CAPEC can support reasoning about robotics security.

papers.title: Exploited Before It Was Fixed? Vulnerability Timelines from Open, Machine-Readable Evidence
papers.summary: -05-X-03), Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalogs, and exploitation sightings. We introduce an evidence model implemented in Vulnerability-Lookup that selects the earliest evidence for each lifecycle event, distinguishes vulnerability-specific records, preserves date precision, and ensures traceability to original sources. Among 3,758 vulnerability identifiers with exploitation evidence, 98% have disclosure dates, while only 15.7% have patch evidence. Vendor-side dates required by VTEM are entirely absent. Most exploitation dates originate from catalog listings, including 1,041 entries associated with bulk catalog imports. After excluding these entries and ambiguous same-day observations, 59 vulnerabilities exhibit patch evidence following exploitation evidence, with a median interval of 7.6 days, predominantly between catalog listings and distributor fixes. Evidence traceability also exposes systematic measurement errors: one collector incorrectly classified exploit publications as active exploitation, accounting for 40% of initial exploitation dates, while another catalog assigned vulnerability publication timestamps to 11% of its listings. Our findings demonstrate that exploitation-to-patch intervals are computationally measurable, but their reliability depends on the availability, precision, and provenance of published evidence. We identify the additional disclosure, exploitation observation, and patch availability timestamps needed to improve vulnerability lifecycle measurements.

papers.title: How Well Is My Artwork Protected? Predicting and Tailoring Protection against Style Mimicry by Personalization
papers.summary: Protection tools add an imperceptible perturbation to each artwork so that a model personalized on it fails to imitate its style, and they apply one recipe, a protection method at a fixed strength, to every artwork. We find that the same recipe protects artworks very differently, well beyond the noise of personalization seeds, and that cheap signals predict this protection before any personalization. Because protection rises and falls together across recipes, our method, Patina, predicts the protection of every recipe from one short trial protection and gives each artwork the weakest recipe whose predicted protection reaches a chosen level. At the same level of visibility, Patina lets more artworks pass the protection threshold than any single recipe and warns the artist about artworks for which no recipe is predicted to pass it.

papers.title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors
papers.summary: Tool-using language-model agents must act on information from untrusted emails, webpages, and documents. This creates a central security challenge: malicious instructions and legitimate task directives can arrive through the same interaction channel. Existing defenses are largely hand-designed and static, making further improvements dependent on repeated manual redesign. We introduce Evolution Under Fire, a staged framework that couples safety-harness evolution with adaptive stressor evolution. Utility-constrained, Pareto-scheduled tree search evolves complete executable safety harnesses from execution evidence while keeping the task model, benchmark, tools, and evaluator fixed. Adaptive stressor evolution then discovers utility-preserving attacks that guide a subsequent stage of harness evolution. On AgentDyn with GPT-4o-mini, an evolved harness reduces attack success from 50.4% to 3.0%, improves clean and attacked utility over the initial harness, and offers a stronger security-utility trade-off than reproduced defenses. On Agent-SafetyBench with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, harness evolution reduces attack success from 82.6% to 62.0% while retaining helpfulness and runtime validity. Evolved harnesses also transfer without further evolution to Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, reducing attack success from 32.1% to 0.9% while improving attacked-task utility.

papers.title: Adaptive LLM-Driven Honeypots vs. LLM-Driven Attackers: Does Narrative Coherence Improve Deception?
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) enable honeypots to generate responses and deceptive artefacts on demand, yet existing approaches evaluate generated content one reply at a time and leave open whether artefacts that jointly describe a coherent event retain an attacker better than unrelated ones. This question becomes pressing as autonomous LLM-driven offensive agents emerge as realistic adversaries. This paper proposes narrative deception, a reactive strategy in which the defender maps each observed attacker command to a MITRE ATT&CK technique, selects a compatible scenario from a curated catalogue based on MITRE Engage, and deploys mutually referential artefacts (files, processes, services, and logs) on an emulated Ubuntu host while the intrusion is under way.
